description: Ex-RAF Hunter later ex-Royal Jordanian Air Force 841 (RJAF serials were retained by Oman). Damaged beyond repair and written off 7 April 1991 per dstorm.eu; preserved in the outdoor display at Bait Al Falaj. Photographed by Dave Hedges 7 Oct 2017 (ABPic, c/n quoted as 8964 - unverified). aviationmuseum.eu lists it as a Hunter F.6 841; ABPic and dstorm.eu give FGA.73B. Sultan of Oman's Air Force (SOAF) camouflage.

BAC 167 Strikemaster Mk 82A, c/n PS.349 (ABPic). Ex-Sultan of Oman's Air Force. Listed as preserved at the SOAF Museum, Bait Al Falaj in the bacstrikemaster.co.uk survivors list (c.2010) and dstorm.eu; photographed on display 7 Oct 2017 (ABPic, Dave Hedges). aviationmuseum.eu gives the serial as 023, which appears to be a typo for 423.

Ex-Sultan of Oman's Air Force / RAFO Skyvan 3M-400, c/n SH1877 (ABPic). Photographed preserved in the outdoor display 7 Oct 2017 (ABPic, Dave Hedges); also listed by aviationmuseum.eu. Tripadvisor reviewer Dec 2018 mentions the Skyvan on display.
aliases: Skyvan; SC7; SH1877; Skyvan 3M; SC.7 Skyvan

description: Agusta-Bell 205A, c/n 4156 (ABPic), ex-Sultan of Oman's Air Force. Photographed preserved in the outdoor display 7 Oct 2017 (ABPic, Dave Hedges); listed by aviationmuseum.eu. Tripadvisor reviews mention a Bell helicopter in the grounds.
aliases: AB205; AB-205A; Bell 205; UH-1H; 4156; AB205A; UH1H

description: Ex-British Army Air Corps Beaver AL.1 XP824, c/n 1489, photographed at RAF Leuchars 1970-71 (ABPic). Now preserved at Bait Al Falaj wearing code / Omani serial 213 (ABPic 'Code Number: 213'; aviationmuseum.eu lists '213 DHC-2 Beaver AL.1'). Photographed 7 Oct 2017 (ABPic, Dave Hedges). True identity XP824 per ABPic; the painted marking 213 has not been independently verified.

Ex-RAF Provost T.1 XF868, c/n PAC/F/057, later UK civil G-BGSB. ABPic records it preserved at the Sultan's Armed Forces Museum (photos 16 Mar 2016 Jean Marc Braun and 7 Oct 2017 Dave Hedges) with 'Code Number XF868' - i.e. it wears its RAF serial; aviationmuseum.eu lists 'XF868 Percival Provost T.1'. Represents the Provost T.52s that were the first SOAF combat aircraft in 1959. Which marking is actually painted on the airframe (XF868 or a SOAF serial) should be confirmed on site.
aliases: Provost T1; G-BGSB; PAC/F/057; Piston Provost; P.56 Provost
